correctness.rationale: For every m≥3 and finite field F_q of characteristic two, the first square defect of f=t+a t^{r+1}+… is (r+1)a² t^{2r+1}. Even shallow r therefore fail. For odd r, f commutes with f², forcing the first nonzero defect to have even degree, while the degree-k even defect depends affinely with coefficient a≠0 on a_{k−r}; one coefficient is uniquely solved per even obstruction. Counting gives the stated depth formula and parity totals. Conditional asymptotic follows from the plateau carrying 1−O(1/m) of the mass. Exhaustive independent substitution checks q=2,4,8,16 at stated degrees support but do not substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: Originality is relative to independently read comparison material, not a uniqueness certificate. The prior all-level theorem addresses only depth one (a proper specialization); the exact all-depth histogram and uniform limiting break law are not implied by the stated depth-one result. value.rationale: The finite Nottingham groups and their ramification filtration are natural in modular group theory and local-field automorphisms. A complete depth-resolved involution census for all quotient levels and all binary finite fields distinguishes genuine formal torsion from nonliftable finite jets, reveals sharp forbidden-even and equal-odd strata, and yields a nondegenerate limiting break distribution. This is not a trivial renaming or numerical extension of the already known depth-one theorem.
